name: Ninja Turtle
beta: Begin in the slim crack that Easy Day uses, then go straight up the face to the bolt anchors. Step right past a roof and continue on a steep face.
overview: Departs from Easy Day's crack onto the face above, heading directly for bolt anchors. Beyond, it swings rightward past a roof and keeps going on a steep face.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Inside the slim crack where Easy Day begins

name: Nobody's Right Mind
beta: Follow the right-hand crack, passing a bolt of some age partway along, and keep to that same crack higher until it reaches the boulders on the crag's right shoulder.
overview: The right-hand of two cracks; one old bolt sits partway up, and the crack ends at boulders on the crag's right-hand shoulder.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Bohemian Bypass
beta: Place gear up to four inches for the first fifteen feet, then clip nine bolts; extend the left-hand part of the route with long slings to keep rope drag down.
overview: Opens on natural protection for about 15 ft, then continues on bolts. Long slings help with drag on the left side.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Rackless Crack
beta: Sharp edges make for pleasant climbing, and it is much easier than Little Roof. Normally led on its three bolts, though small gear works too.
overview: Pleasant sharp edges; normally led clipping the bolts, though small natural gear also works. Noticeably simpler than Little Roof, the other 5.10d crack.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: North Face
beta: Start atop a boulder that leans against the face and go straight up past a string of bolts plus a fixed piton. Veer left past more bolts, turn the corner onto the northeast shoulder, and continue to the top.
overview: An old ladder of bolts on the north prow, launched from a boulder propped against the wall. After a fixed piton and several bolts it veers left, rounds the corner onto the northeast shoulder, and ends in a bold, loose finish.

current.location: north prow, roughly 40 ft over from the Northwest Face, on its left side, starting on a boulder propped against the wall

name: Northwest Face
beta: Climb straight up the line of bolts; a few of the older hangers only accept small-gate carabiners, so bring a couple of those.
overview: A long-standing aid line on North Yak's northwest side, now climbed as a bolt ladder that can go free. Its bolts have seen heavy use over the years, and it is regarded as a classic of the crag.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Not Just another Pretty Face
beta: Start on a ledge a few feet right of Marchesa, pass an old bolt that has lost its hanger, then trace a seam up to the next ledge. The gear is more reassuring than it appears.
overview: Starts on a ledge, passes a bolt with no hanger and then a seam to a ledge; gear is better than it appears.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: on a ledge, 5 ft to the right of Marchesa

name: Oatmeal Eating Aardvarks
beta: Boulder onto the ledge at its right-hand side, then follow three bolts up the face. Originally done without protection bolts; they went in later.
overview: Boulder onto the ledge from the right, then pass a trio of bolts. The first ascent had no bolts; they came later.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: west face of the tower: get onto the ledge at its right end

name: Oddjob
beta: Two bolts on the north face of a pale boulder. The tricky start comes before the first clip, so stick-clipping it is a sensible alternative to bouldering up.
overview: Two bolts, with a scary bouldery start to the first; a stick-clip is an alternative.

current.area_walk_in: The two brown boulders lie downhill and right along the slope; the pale boulder with this route stands just ahead of them.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: north wall of a pale boulder that stands ahead of the brown ones

name: Odds And Sods
beta: Climb the slab directly past its four bolts.
overview: A slab route on the right-hand edge of the face, starting well left of a big left-facing corner. Four bolts protect the face moves.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: slab on the far-right portion of the face, well left of a big corner

name: Omega
beta: Take the lengthy gully that slants rightward across the left portion of the north face. Several optional starts lead into it, ranging from an easy crack to a bolted harder start. The only real difficulty is a single overhang higher up, which can be passed several ways, then the gully continues to the top.
overview: A lengthy gully slanting rightward on the north side. Several alternate starts sit beside it, then an overhang provides the only hard moves before the gully carries on to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: lengthy gully tilting rightward, toward the left part of the north face

name: Only Outlaws Have Guns
beta: Three bolts lead up the face right of its neighbour; at the top move right to reach the rappel anchors.
overview: Three bolts guard this face line; finish by traversing rightward to the rappel anchors.

current.area_walk_in: The trail reaches the wall at its right end, so you meet the routes in the reverse of their listed left-to-right order.

name: Oona Kuma
beta: Begin about fifteen feet from the neighbouring route and angle rightward, picking up a bolt that belongs to Yabba Dabba Dudes; keep traversing until the third bolt, then head vertically to the shared chains.
overview: A bolted face line (roughly 15 ft over from The Quarry, trending right via the lowest clip of Yabba Dabba Dudes). Clip 7 bolts on the way up.

current.anchor: 2-bolt anchor also used by Yabba Dabba Dudes
current.location: roughly 15 ft over from The Quarry, trending right via the lowest clip of Yabba Dabba Dudes

name: Outhouse Flake
beta: Enter a notch hidden behind a little pinnacle and climb a wide, left-leaning flake crack. There is nothing to place for protection.
overview: A wide, leftward-slanting crack formed by a flake, entered through a gap behind a little pinnacle; essentially unprotectable.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 20 ft up and over to the right of Frostline, at a gap hidden behind a little spire

name: Overhang Bypass
beta: Take the middle one of three tight chutes. Continue up and rightward to a flake and roof over a cave; going right around it is easiest, though you can also pass it via the left side or directly across. Reach a ledge under the summit roof, shuffle rightward beneath it, and clip the bolt protecting the last slab moves.
overview: Centre chute of three narrow ones, then a flake and roof sitting over a cave, to a ledge under the top bulge; a sideways hand traverse under it ends at a single bolt covering final friction moves.

name: Overnight Sensation
beta: Climb leftward-leaning cracks to the left edge of a brown scoop, then up into a second big scoop and finish via a crack slanting right. One of the original four bolts appears to be gone.
overview: Leftward-leaning cracks take you to the left edge of a brown, hollowed patch, then into a second big hollow, and a crack slanting right finishes it.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Overpowered By Funk
beta: Narrow cracks then open face all the way, with a single bolt about fifteen feet off the ground; stay with the crack system to the top.
overview: A highly regarded line of narrow cracks and face moves. It was top-roped first and led several years later.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Papal Smear
beta: Follow the crack a few feet from The Popemobile, clip the single bolt high on the route, and merge with that line where it clips the rounded arete above.
overview: Crack climbing that clips one bolt up high, then converges with the neighbouring line at its bolt on the rounded arete.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: crack roughly 6 ft to the right of The Popemobile

name: Paranoia
beta: Four bolts lead up the left line; it shares its first bolt with the right-hand route.
overview: The left one of two bolted lines on a V-shaped face, on the towers' eastern flank.

current.location: left-hand line on a V-shaped wall, on the Stirrup Towers' east flank

name: Party in the Desert
beta: Begin a few feet right of the previous route with a thin crack, then angle up and leftward past three bolts.
overview: A thin crack begins things, then the line drifts up and left past three bolts.

name: Passion Play
beta: Two bolts protect the moves up the water streak, ending at the bolt cluster at the top that serves as the belay.
overview: A short, starred streak of dark rock standing in the creek bed. Pleasant, enjoyable moves lead to a cluster of old bolts that make up the belay.

current.location: Brief wet streak up a creekside boulder beyond the second footbridge, directly facing The Shepherd

name: Flying Dutchman
beta: Stand on a heap of small stones to begin, then ascend a steep crack; low down you will find a pair of bolts plus a fixed nut.
overview: A sustained steep crack, with a pair of bolts and a nut left in place low on the line.

overview: Begins in a short corner up to a ledge, then crosses the overhead roof at a bolt.

overview: Climbs a shallow water-worn chute up to a ledge, then switches to the central chute above, passing a bolt on the way to the top.

overview: A dangerous little climb: surmount a crumbly bulge to reach its single bolt, then move diagonally upward and rightward, with a long unprotected stretch to the finish.

name: Pictures at an Exhibition
beta: Follow the dike straight up, clipping three bolts.
overview: A dike system on the formation's northern tip, climbed past bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Take the nature trail northeast, crest a rise and pass a marker, then after roughly 100 yards swing left over flat slabs and head southwest into a brushy, boulder-strewn valley. Where it opens (Lost Corridor) bear right into a tighter passage that pinches very narrow; when it widens, the Corridor Face is the wall on your left. A more direct option starts below the Pathetic routes and heads northeast via a rocky passage.

name: Pie Crust

overview: A traditional face line. The hard part: difficult face finish above easy flakes.

overview: Three bolts on the left of the crag beside a reddish arete, followed by slanting cracks to the right and a higher horizontal back left before topping out.
